A1.justification: Both PDFs describe VCG-Bench and contain complete, readable main text and Appendices A–F. All 37 pages were compared: pages 2–37 match in text and rendering; page 1 adds project access information and updates date/version markings.

before.justification: v1 reports original diagram-generation and editing experiments in Section 6, including Tables 7–10, plus baseline comparisons, robustness analyses, and a human audit in Appendix A.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experimental results in Section 6 and Appendix A, including quantitative model comparisons and supplementary evaluations.

M1.justification: The diagram-generation pipeline, incremental XML patching procedure, data-construction process, and validation components are unchanged, including their specifications and prompts in the appendices.

E1.justification: Both versions retain the same 1,449-diagram dataset spanning six domains and 15 subdomains, the same generation and editing tasks, and the same supplementary evaluation scenarios.

E2.justification: The evaluated model rosters in corresponding tables are identical. The Paper2Any comparison in Appendix A.1.1 and pixel-based editing baseline in Appendix A.1.6 are present in both versions without revision.

E3.justification: Evaluation metrics, sample subsets, difficulty definitions, temperature settings, image-plus-caption generation inputs, and XML patch editing protocols are unchanged in Sections 4–6 and the appendices.

E4.justification: Both versions contain the same caption ablation, cross-judge SCS validation, difficulty and error analyses, qualitative examples, and XDRFR human correction audit. No analysis is added or removed.

E5.justification: Table 5 retains the same mean-and-standard-deviation reporting on the shared valid subset of 78 examples. No repeated-run, seed, confidence-interval, or significance-reporting changes appear elsewhere.

E6.justification: All numerical and qualitative results are unchanged, including Appendix A. For example, Gemini-3-Pro retains Task-1 SCS of 0.7790 in Table 7 and Task-2 XDRFR of 0.9405 in Table 10.

T1.justification: The task definitions in Section 4 and mathematical metric definitions in Section 5 and Appendix F are identical. No assumptions, derivations, theorems, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about a unified multidomain benchmark, editable diagram generation, and limitations of current models. The project-page addition does not alter the scientific contributions.

C2.justification: Interpretations of the generation–editing capability gap and SCS judge dependence are unchanged. The limitations concerning mxGraph-only coverage, underrepresented labels/styles, ambiguous edits, and real-world applicability are also retained.

D1.justification: v2 adds an explicit project-page URL beneath the authors on page 1, supplying access information absent from v1. Implementation details, prompts, and release/licensing statements are unchanged; the PDFs do not establish what resources are available at that address.

R1.justification: Section 2, the benchmark-positioning comparison in Table 2, and the references are unchanged. The added link points to this project's page and does not revise its relationship to prior research.

P1.justification: The front matter gains a project-page line and updated preprint/arXiv date and version text. There are no body-text rewrites, terminology changes, or section reorganizations.

P2.justification: Page 1 adds a centered project-page line below the authors and updates the margin version stamp. Figures 1–10 and Tables 1–13 retain their content and design; pages 2–37 render identically.

improvement.justification: The new project-page pointer modestly improves resource discoverability over v1's release statements without an explicit project address. Scientific content and supporting evidence, including all appendices, are unchanged. This benefit concerns access documentation; the PDFs alone do not verify code or data availability.
